title: Intervals, Thresholds, and Long Slow Distance: the Role of Intensity and Duration in Endurance Training
claims: Elite endurance athletes perform 80% or more of their training at intensities clearly below lactate threshold and use high-intensity training sparingly.
Analysis of more than 15,000 training sessions across three world and/or Olympic champions found about 85% of sessions were continuous low-to-moderate work at or below 2 mmol/L blood lactate.

About 80% of training sessions are performed completely or predominantly below the first ventilatory turn point or at a blood lactate concentration of about 2 mM; the remaining approximately 20% is distributed between threshold work and 90-100% VO2max intervals.
Adding high-intensity training three to four times per week for several weeks can temporarily suppress performance and induce overreaching.
Studies involving intensification of training in already well-trained athletes have shown equivocal results at best.
